source_text: Ἔνθεν δὲ καὶ ἄθεοι κεκλήμεθα· καὶ ὁμολογοῦμεν τῶν τοιούτων νομιζομένων θεῶν ἄθεοι εἶναι, ἀλλ᾿ οὐχὶ τοῦ ἀληθεστάτου καὶ πατρὸς δικαιοσύνης καὶ σωφροσύνης καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἀρετῶν ἀνεπιμίκτου τε κακίας θεοῦ· ἀλλ᾿ ἐκεῖνόν τε καὶ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ υἱὸν ἐλθόντα καὶ διδάξαντα ἡμᾶς ταῦτα, καὶ τὸν τῶν ἄλλων ἑπομένων καὶ ἐξομοιουμένων ἀγαθῶν ἀγγέλων στρατόν, πνεῦμά τε τὸ προφητικὸν σεβόμεθα καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν, λόγῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ τιμῶντες, καὶ παντὶ βουλομένῳ μαθεῖν, ὡς ἐδιδάχθημεν, ἀφθόνως παραδιδόντες.
pass_a_gloss: From this also we are called atheists; and we confess to be atheists of such gods as are thought to be, but not of the truest and Father of justice and self-control and the other virtues and unmingled with evil God; but that one and the Son coming from Him and teaching us these things, and the army of good angels following and being conformed to them, and the prophetic Spirit we reverence and worship, honoring with word and truth, and to all who wish to learn, as we were taught, we give abundantly
pass_b_english: It is for this reason that we are called atheists, and we acknowledge that we are atheists with respect to the gods commonly believed to exist. Yet we are not atheists with respect to the truest God, the Father of justice and self‑control and the other virtues, the God completely unmingled with evil. That God we revere and worship, along with His Son who came from Him and taught us these things, and the host of good angels who follow and are conformed to them, and the prophetic Spirit. We honor them with word and truth, and we pass on these teachings freely to anyone who wishes to learn, just as we ourselves were taught.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex syntax of the Greek, particularly the distinction between the false gods and the true God, and the subsequent list of objects of reverence (Son, angels, Spirit). Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
